To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the first principal component of mfVEP is a V1 component, which reverses in polarity above and below, and across, the midline and vertical meridians respectively, and that this component can be used to reconstruct a coronal section through V1.
a principal component analysis of the local mfVEP responses can be applied to three-channel recordings, and that the first principal components are consistent with the distribution of V1.

a principal component analysis of the multifocal visual evoked potential (mfVEP), with three channels, can be used to derive a component that is similar to the VEP obtained with a full-field pattern reversal stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of pattern reversal mfVEP to the diagnosis of visual field defects.
the development of an approach to the study of the human visual cortex based on the analysis of the mfVEP.
the use of mfVEP to investigate the topographical distribution of V1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this approach is useful in the study of VEPs and that the first principal component of VEP responses is a useful tool to investigate the visual pathways and the visual cortex.
the first principal component is the best candidate for the V1 component.
the first principal component of the mfVEP is a V1 component.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the first principal component of the mfVEP is a V1 response.

the mfVEP is a useful tool for the evaluation of visual function in patients with visual field defects and that the first principal component of the mfVEP may be used for the construction of the V1 map.
a principal component analysis of mfVEPs can provide a means for the construction of an anatomical map of the visual field representation within the occipital lobe.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the first principal component of the mfVEP is a useful tool to identify the location of V1 in a coronal section.
the first principal component of multifocal VEPs can be used to derive the location of the primary visual cortex.
a simple model based on a principal component analysis can provide a useful approximation of the V1 component of mfVEP recordings.
